sources.title: Our hiring process - Google Careers
sources.basis: Google's own careers page on its hiring process
sources.summary: Names the stages: Google Hiring Assessment (workstyle) plus role-related assessments such as a coding exercise, one or two recruiter conversations, optional project work, then a panel of structured interviews scored on shared rubrics with open-ended role-related questions, no brainteasers, AI tools not permitted; roughly 6-8 weeks.

sources.title: Interviewing at Google: Best practices, advice, and tips - Google Careers
sources.basis: Google's own careers page on how to prepare for its interviews
sources.summary: Google's interview advice: questions are largely 'Tell me about a time...' and 'How would you approach...', STAR structure, data-backed impact ('Accomplished X, as measured by Y, by doing Z'), ambiguity, conflict with a co-worker, influencing teammates, leadership style; notes internal review after interviews and that Search/AI are not permitted.

sources.title: A guide to structured interviewing for better hiring practices - Google re:Work
sources.basis: Google's own published guide to how it runs structured interviews
sources.summary: How Google structures interviews: vetted role-relevant questions, recorded feedback, rubrics graded poor/borderline/solid/outstanding; hiring attributes role-related knowledge, problem solving, leadership (emergent leadership for ICs); one behavioural and one hypothetical example question, each with its predetermined follow-ups.

sources.title: My Google [ Software Engineer ] Interview Experience | L4
sources.basis: The author's own free Medium post, cited and linked
sources.summary: 2025 L4 loop, one phone screen plus three technical rounds and a Googliness round, with the questions: arrange item quantities in an m x n grid so like items are adjacent; safe deletion order for disks and snapshots (dependency graph); maximum nesting of 2D boxes (hard DP); reshuffle blocks of coloured houses so each block is unique and sorted. Says 'exceeds' was needed in two of three technical rounds.

sources.title: Google L5 interview experience
sources.basis: The author's own free Medium post, cited and linked
sources.summary: L5 loop: phone screen coded in a Google Doc, then five virtual onsite rounds (three coding, one system design, one Googleyness and Leadership); recruiter's topic list; coding rounds on a geometry problem and a DFS graph problem with a scheduling follow-up; design an image/GIF/video hosting platform without sign-up; G&L questions on failure, others' impact on your success, pushing back on a manager's technical decision.

sources.title: Google Interview Experience - L4 Software Engineer
sources.basis: The author's own Substack post, cited and linked
sources.summary: 2022 L4 loop, five rounds with the question type for each: screening round on a priority queue, multi-source BFS, a modified Dijkstra, a vague overlapping-intervals variant with four escalating follow-ups, and a Googlyness round (resolving a conflict between teammates, onboarding a new joiner). Older than three years.

sources.title: SDE II Interview Prep
sources.basis: Amazon's own careers page on how it interviews SDE II candidates
sources.summary: SDE II process: application, online assessment (90 minutes for two coding questions, then system design scenarios and a Work Style Survey on the Leadership Principles), then a loop of four 55-minute interviews; at least one system design question; syntactically correct code, no pseudocode; two or three Leadership Principle behavioural questions per interviewer, STAR, no brain teasers; outcome within 5 business days.

sources.title: SDE III Interview Prep
sources.basis: Amazon's own careers page on how it interviews senior SDE (SDE III) candidates
sources.summary: Senior SDE process: a 60-minute technical phone screen with a senior leader (half Leadership Principles, half coding and system design), then a loop of five 55-minute interviews covering technical and Leadership Principle competencies; at least one system design question, high-level and low-level design; syntactically correct code.

sources.title: Interview Loop
sources.basis: Amazon's own careers page on its interview loop
sources.summary: The loop: two to seven interviewers, possibly including a Bar Raiser from another team focused on hiring quality, 45-60 minutes each; behavioural questions guided by the Leadership Principles, no brain teasers; five example questions (a problem with multiple possible solutions, a risk/mistake/failure, leading a project, motivating a group, using data to decide); STAR. The body sits in collapsed sections rendered from embedded script data, so a plain GET sees only headings.

sources.title: Leadership Principles
sources.basis: Amazon's own careers page stating the Leadership Principles its behavioural interviews assess
sources.summary: Full text of all sixteen Leadership Principles (Customer Obsession through Success and Scale Bring Broad Responsibility), the rubric for every behavioural question in the loop.

sources.title: Interview Experience — SDE-2 at Amazon (Accepted offer)
sources.basis: The author's own free Medium post, cited and linked
sources.summary: SDE-2 (L5) loop: OA (task-scheduler-style problem and a DP problem, plus behavioural), coding round (nodes at a given level of an N-ary tree, then O(1) counts under inserts/deletes), LLD (design Stack Overflow in 30 minutes), HLD with the hiring manager (design an online coding judge), Bar Raiser (40 minutes of LPs then trapping rain water); names the two LPs asked in each round.

sources.title: My Amazon Sde 1 Interview Experience
sources.basis: The author's own free Medium post, cited and linked
sources.summary: SDE-1, Sept 2025 to Feb 2026: 70-minute HackerRank OA (two DSA problems, work simulation, workstyle); round 2 stock-trading DP and trapping rain water plus a project deep-dive; round 3 rotting oranges and maximal rectangle of 1s plus Kafka ordering/partitioning and B vs B+ trees; Bar Raiser on Leadership Principles with three to four levels of follow-up.

sources.title: My Amazon SDE-1 Interview Experience
sources.basis: The author's own free Medium post, cited and linked
sources.summary: SDE-1, four rounds: OA (two DP problems, behavioural judgement scenarios); round 1 minimum classrooms for lecture timings with a follow-up to assign rooms, plus design an automated restaurant system; round 2 inorder traversal, subtree of another tree, and a rotting-vegetables multi-source BFS; Bar Raiser with 35-40 minutes of behavioural questions then a LiveCode problem.

sources.title: Technical interviewing | Microsoft Careers
sources.basis: Microsoft's own careers page on how it runs technical interviews
sources.summary: Describes the 45-minute technical round using a third-party coding tool, and the four things engineering interviewers assess: problem solving ('how you break down information...how you put yourself in the customer's shoes'), design (building/designing a system from scratch), coding (clean, concise, bug-free code in your strongest language), and testing (corner cases, security, error conditions).

sources.title: How we hire | Microsoft Careers
sources.basis: Microsoft's own careers page describing its hiring process end to end
sources.summary: Stages from application to offer: application review with an optional screening conversation, then 2-4 interviews of up to an hour each by phone, Teams, or in person, then an offer stage covering total compensation, then pre-onboarding logistics.

sources.title: Software Engineer 2 UI Interview at Microsoft
sources.basis: The author's own dev.to post, cited and linked
sources.summary: SE2 (UI/frontend) loop at Microsoft IDC Bangalore, six rounds: 2-hour machine coding (build an email client or chat UI in vanilla JS); JS round (write an ES6/ES2020 polyfill, a Promise-based LRU memoization); HLD+LLD design a Snakes and Ladders game; two string/backtracking DSA problems; hiring-manager round on JS, performance and web vitals; final round with senior leadership on DS and system design. Older than three years but specific.

sources.title: What I learned after failing a technical interview at Microsoft
sources.basis: The author's own dev.to post, cited and linked
sources.summary: June 2022 SDE II loop, three rounds (one behavioural, two coding on Microsoft Teams). Names the two LeetCode-medium coding questions asked: 'Kth Largest Element in an Array' and 'Longest substring with no repeating characters'; author failed on communication (no clarifying questions, no discussion of alternatives) despite solving both optimally.

sources.title: My Microsoft SDE Interview Experience as a Fresher (2026)
sources.basis: The author's own first-person blog post, cited and linked; robots.txt allows /blog/*
sources.summary: Fresher SDE loop: online assessment (an array problem, a tree-traversal variant, CS-fundamentals MCQs); first technical round (an array problem with a memory-constraint follow-up); second technical round (an ambiguous notification-system design prompt); final HR/project round on the candidate's college scheduling tool.

sources.title: Preparing for your software engineering interview at Meta | Meta Careers
sources.basis: Meta's own careers page on how it runs software engineering interviews
sources.summary: Two-stage process: initial technical screen (intros, 35 minutes of coding on algorithms/data structures/recursion/binary trees, questions); then a full loop of three 45-minute interviews (a harder coding round, a design round done on a whiteboard covering systems or product, and a behavioural round on background/passion/fit using STAR). Advises writing code in a plain text editor without syntax highlighting.

sources.title: Meta Jobs Hiring Process | Meta Careers
sources.basis: Meta's own careers page on its end-to-end hiring process
sources.summary: Stages: application, an initial recruiter call on background/experience/goals, a recruiter conversation plus initial screening plus a full loop interview (assessing technical background and problem solving), a decision from the recruiter, then an offer letter; typically 2-3 months end to end.

sources.title: Meta Three-Round Interview Experience: Finally Landing the IC5 Position!
sources.basis: The author's own dev.to post recounting their own IC5 loop, cited and linked
sources.summary: IC5 loop, three rounds after an 8-week process: coding round designing a program that ingests two CSV files of dinosaur data to compute speed and sort bipedal dinosaurs; behavioural round on conflict resolution, tight deadlines, and team leadership; system design round to 'Design FB Post Search' with sub-500ms median query latency and content searchable within a minute of posting.

sources.title: [2025][Meta] E4 Production Engineer Interview Experience
sources.basis: The author's own first-person Substack post, cited and linked; robots.txt's User-agent: * block does not disallow /p/ post paths (only /p/*/comment/*)
sources.summary: E4 Production Engineer loop: phone screen with a CSV-parsing/string-manipulation coding problem and a website-outage troubleshooting exercise (root cause: disk space); onsite of four rounds - coding with optimisation follow-ups, system design (author's weakest round), Linux fundamentals (memory management, processes, file systems, security, networking), and a STAR-format behavioural round.

sources.title: Netflix Culture | Careers at Netflix
sources.basis: Netflix's own careers page setting out the hiring and evaluation philosophy it applies to candidates and employees
sources.summary: States the 'keeper test' used in hiring and retention decisions ('if X wanted to leave, would I fight to keep them?'), that the Dream Team is 'driven by performance, not seniority, tenure, or unconditional loyalty', and the eight core traits Netflix hires and evaluates for: judgment, communication, curiosity, courage, passion, selflessness, innovation, and inclusion.

sources.title: How We Hire | NVIDIA
sources.basis: NVIDIA's own careers page describing its hiring process
sources.summary: Three-stage process: search and apply (recommends applying to at most five best-matched roles); 'Let's Meet' - phone/video/in-person rounds with the hiring manager, team members and other groups, a mandatory in-person onsite before any offer, a HackerRank coding exercise for technical roles (explicitly disqualifies use of unapproved tools like ChatGPT during the interview), and an optional 15-minute non-evaluative 'Insider Chat' with an employee resource group member; then join-the-team logistics. Decisions typically communicated within a few weeks.

sources.title: How We Hire at Salesforce | Interviewing at Salesforce
sources.basis: Salesforce's own careers page on its hiring process
sources.summary: Most interviews happen virtually over Google Meet with candidates expected to be on camera; an on-site office interview is required before any offer; interviewers may ask behavioural, competency-based, or situational questions; states a merit-based, non-discriminatory hiring policy and recommends applying to no more than three roles in a 12-month period.

sources.title: Interview Experience with Salesforce
sources.basis: The author's own dev.to post, cited and linked
sources.summary: First-round MTS interview conducted by a senior manager overseeing two teams; the round centred on the candidate's recent work experience, how they handle on-call support, and their approach to production issues under pressure, rather than DSA questions. Only the first round is described.

sources.title: How We Hire | Adobe
sources.basis: Adobe's own careers page on its hiring process
sources.summary: Five-step process: application; a talent-partner conversation on background and career goals; a hiring-manager interview on problem-solving and fit; skills assessments and team interviews (for technical roles: 'coding challenges, system design discussions, or portfolio reviews'); then offer, background checks and onboarding.

sources.title: Web Engineer Intern at Adobe - Interview
sources.basis: The author's own dev.to post, cited and linked
sources.summary: Web Engineer intern loop: HackerRank OA (one LeetCode-medium problem, 45 minutes); a resume/skills-and-interests round with an engineering manager; three back-to-back technical rounds (JS-based DSA plus DOM manipulation; React fundamentals and architecture; testing frameworks plus behavioural); same-day recruiter behavioural call; offer three days later. Notes Adobe's process is team-dependent, not standardised. Older than three years but specific.
